title: Sheaf Ext of coherent modules is coherent
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Then for every integer $q$ the sheaf Ext $\mathcal Ext^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext] is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma lemma-coherent-internal-hom (Tag 0D0C), applied to K = F[0] in D^-_Coh and L = G[0] in D^+_Coh: RHom(F,G) lies in D^+_Coh, so its cohomology sheaves Ext^q(F,G) are coherent

proof.text: At each point choose an affine neighbourhood inside a finite generating neighbourhood of F. Local Noetherianity makes its coordinate ring Noetherian; quasi-coherence and finite type identify F with the tilde of a finite module. Resolve that module by finite free modules and sheafify. The private local_free_resolution repeats the construction of lem-sc-coherent-affine-free-resolution with only IsLocallyNoetherian: its construction needs no compactness. Obtain a bounded-above finite free resolution on the over-site of the chosen open, and transport it to the open subscheme through overEquiv.

Compute sheaf Ext by a bounded-below injective resolution I of G[0]. The private local_homology_model generalizes the existing scalar computation to the arbitrary coefficient G. Restriction preserves K-injectives and commutes with the ordinary Hom complex. The representative comparison for derivedInternalHom, exactness of restriction, and homologyFunctorFactors identify restricted sheaf Ext with H^q Hom(E,G|U[0]); derivedInternalHom_of_boundedAbove_finiteFree removes I. Computation on U uses the standard derived-category universe and hence applies to the arbitrary ambient universe in the theorem.

source.place: 08DL, restriction of RHom; 0GM8, bounded-above finite free computation

proof.text: Hom(E,G|U[0]) is the signed dual complex with term Hom(E^(-i),G|U). Since E^(-i) is finite free of rank r, this term is a finite direct sum of copies of G|U, hence coherent. Its degree-q homology is the cokernel of the map from the preceding term into the kernel of the next differential. Closure of coherent modules under kernels, cokernels, finite sums and isomorphisms makes this homology coherent in every integer degree, without a separate negative-degree case. Coherence descends from the open cover. Zero ranks and empty schemes are included by finite sum and cover locality.
